turns.content: Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Sarah. What's going on?
I've just been feeling a bit anxious lately, especially about starting this new blog on mental health.
That sounds like a big step. What makes you feel anxious about it?
I worry that I'm not experienced enough to speak on such important topics or that no one will relate to my experiences.
It's completely normal to have doubts when starting something new. But from what I know, you've been through quite a lot, which can give you a deep understanding of mental health.
True... I guess part of me feels that by sharing my journey, it might help others, but I feel vulnerable being so open.
Hey, I just reconnected with an old college friend. It's been a while since we talked.
That sounds intriguing! How did you two get back in touch?
Actually, he stumbled upon my blog about mental health and reached out. We've been catching up a bit.
That's so nice! Your blog must really resonate with people. How are you feeling about reconnecting?
It's been nice, but it's also brought up a lot of past feelings and memories. I guess I'm a bit overwhelmed.
That makes sense. Old friendships can bring up a lot of emotions. How are you managing those feelings?
I'm trying to keep things in perspective and use what I've learned in therapy. It's just...sometimes it feels like too much.
It's good that you're using your therapeutic tools. Have you talked to your therapist about it?
Not yet. We've been focusing more on my recent breakup and the tension with Jack, my boss-slash-partner.
That sounds like it keeps you pretty occupied. It might help to bring this up with your therapist too when you can.
You're right. I think I just needed to talk it out first. Sometimes, these old connections feel a bit disruptive.
I understand that. It’s okay to feel that way. Maybe there's something positive this old friend can bring to your life again?
True, he was really supportive back in college. It’s nice to have that kind of support again.
Absolutely! It's great that you have someone who can be there for you. How do you see things moving forward with him?
I think we'll just take things slow. I'm not sure how much time I can commit with everything else going on.
Taking it slow sounds like a good plan. It's important to prioritize what feels manageable.
Yeah, I'll try to. I want to focus more on the things that lift me up, like my art classes and my blog.
Hey, I hope you're available to chat for a bit. I could use some support right now.
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's been going on?
Well, I finally told my colleague that I have feelings for him, and we decided to start dating.
That's a big step! How are you feeling about it?
I'm feeling a mix of excitement and worry. It's great to be with someone I connect with, but I'm also scared about how things might change at work.
It's understandable to have those mixed feelings. Entering a new relationship is exciting but can also bring changes. What's your biggest concern right now?
I guess I'm worried about how our colleagues might react. We both agreed to keep things professional, but gossip can be brutal.
Office dynamics can be tricky. It sounds like you two have a good plan in place to stay professional. Do you think there's someone in the office you can confide in if things get challenging?
I do have a couple of colleagues who I trust. It's just that my last breakdown at work left me feeling a bit vulnerable. I'm trying to avoid that happening again.
It's great you have people you trust. And remember, you’ve come a long way since that incident. How have you been managing stress since starting therapy?
Therapy has been really helpful. It's taught me ways to set boundaries and be more open about my feelings. I think it’s why I felt ready to approach my colleague.
That's wonderful to hear. Taking those steps for personal growth can really make a difference. Have you talked to your therapist about starting this new relationship?
Not yet, but I'm planning on bringing it up in my next session. My therapist has really helped me gain perspective on my relationships.
That sounds like a great idea. Having professional guidance can really clarify things. How are things on the friendship front with your close friend?
My friend is still struggling, which has been hard to watch. I've been trying to be there for them without overstepping.
It must be tough to see someone you care about go through a hard time. How are you handling being supportive without taking on too much yourself?
I try to listen and offer support when I can but also remind myself that their journey is separate from mine, and I need to set limits for my own well-being.
That's a healthy approach. Remember, you can only do so much, and caring for yourself is crucial. How do you unwind after emotionally exhausting days?
I've been getting into yoga and reading a lot lately. It helps me center myself and escape my thoughts for a while.
Hey, I really need to talk.
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
It's about Mark... he was hospitalized recently due to his mental health. I feel so helpless and worried.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It must be so hard to see someone you care about going through this. How are you holding up?
Honestly, I'm struggling. I want to help, but I'm scared of doing the wrong thing. It's like I'm walking on eggshells.
That sounds really challenging. It's natural to feel unsure, but your concern for Mark shows how much you care. Have you had a chance to talk to him or his doctors?
I haven't yet. I'm afraid of overwhelming him, or saying something that might upset him.
It's understandable to feel that way, but even just letting him know you're there for him can be very comforting. Sometimes just being present is a big support.
You're right. I keep thinking about everything else that's been going on, too. Like the issues at work and my anxiety shooting up lately. It's all piling up.
Hey, I hope you have a moment. I just found out my boss resigned.
Hi Sarah! Of course, I'm here for you. How do you feel about the resignation?
It's kind of a relief but also really unsettling. I didn't expect this to happen so suddenly.
I can imagine it must be quite a mix of emotions. It's understandable to feel both relieved and unsettled.
Yeah, it's like a weight has been lifted, but now I'm anxious about what's next for our team.
It's okay to feel uncertain about the future. It can be tough to navigate such changes, especially after all that's happened.
Thank you for saying that. It helps me not feel so alone in this. I guess I'm also worried about who's going to take over.
That makes sense. Leadership transitions can be challenging and sometimes unpredictable. Are there specific concerns you have about the new boss?
I'm worried someone might come in with the same issues or maybe even make things worse. I just hope we get someone who respects their employees.
Hey, I've been going through a lot lately and could really use someone to talk to.
Hi Sarah, I'm here for you. What's been on your mind?
Well, I've made a big decision to cut down on my working hours.
That's a significant step. How are you feeling about it?
It's a mix of relief and uncertainty. I'm glad to have more time for myself, but I worry about my career.
It's completely normal to feel both relieved and anxious. Taking care of your mental health is crucial though.
You're right. I've been trying to focus more on painting, as it helps with my stress.
That's wonderful. Engaging in a hobby can be so therapeutic. Have you noticed any changes in how you feel since you started painting?
Yes, definitely. It's like I can express what's inside without words, but sometimes the pressures of work still get to me.
It sounds like painting has become an important outlet for you. It's okay if work stress still creeps in; what matters is that you have ways to cope.
Thanks, I keep reminding myself of that. It's hard not to feel like I'm falling behind sometimes.
I understand. You've been through a lot with work and relationships. You're doing your best, and that's enough.
I try to remember that. The therapy sessions have helped too. I just worry about Mark being in the hospital; it brings back old anxieties.
It's tough seeing someone you care about struggle. Have you managed to talk to Mark or visit him?
I did visit him. It was really hard, but I think he appreciated the company. I just wish I could do more.
Sometimes being there is enough. You're a good friend, and your support means a lot to him.
Thanks. I just hope he knows that he's not alone.
I'm sure he does. Keep taking care of yourself too; you need your strength to support others.
I will. Cutting back on work is a start, I suppose.
It absolutely is. It's a brave decision, and shows you're prioritizing your well-being.
Sometimes I just doubt if I'm doing the right thing.
Doubt can be part of the process, but remember that prioritizing yourself isn't wrong.
I guess so. It's just that balancing everything feels overwhelming at times.
Hey Taylor, I just wanted to check in and see how you're doing today?
Hey, thanks for reaching out. I'm not too great, honestly.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
Yeah, I think it might help. I had a fallout with a close classmate over a group project. It’s just really weighing heavily on me.
Hey, I just wanted to talk about something that's been on my mind.
Of course, Taylor. What's been going on?
I've been feeling really stuck and stressed lately. You remember the writer's block I mentioned before? It's still there.
I'm sorry to hear that. It can be so frustrating when creativity feels blocked, especially with everything else you've got going on.
Yeah, it's like I want to write, but every time I try, nothing comes out. Plus, everything that's happened recently hasn't helped.
It sounds like you've been through a lot. That can definitely make it harder to find motivation and focus.
Exactly. Between the argument with my ex, failing that mid-term, and falling out with my classmate... I just feel overwhelmed.
That's a lot to deal with in a short amount of time. It makes sense that you're feeling pressured and overwhelmed.
The only positive thing recently is that I found this online community of writers. They've been really encouraging.
That's wonderful to hear! Having a supportive community can make a huge difference. How have they been helping you?
They've just been really good about listening and offering advice. They're all going through similar struggles, so it's comforting to not feel alone.
Hey, I just need to talk to someone. Is that okay?
Hey, are you online? I really need someone to talk to right now.
Hey, I talked to my siblings today, and it felt really different, but in a good way.
That’s wonderful to hear, Taylor! How did that conversation come about?
I guess I was feeling overwhelmed with everything—school, writing, just life—and I needed someone to turn to. They've been really supportive lately, and I felt I could open up to them.
It sounds like reaching out to your siblings was a brave step. What did you talk about, if you don’t mind sharing?
We talked about all the pressures I've been feeling with my studies and how I've been questioning my direction. I also brought up how the argument between Mom and Dad affected me.
Hey Taylor, I've been thinking about you. How are you holding up today?
Hey... It's been a rough day. I found out my close friend was hospitalized, and it just feels like too much right now.
I'm so sorry to hear about your friend. That must be really hard to process. Do you want to talk more about it?
Yeah, it's just...she've always been there for me, especially through the whole thing with my ex and when I was struggling at school. It feels surreal not being able to support her now.
It sounds like they mean a lot to you, and not being able to be there for her must be really tough. It’s understandable to feel overwhelmed.
Exactly. And it's like all these emotions from the past are surfacing again - the argument with my parents, the panic attacks, the trust issues with my professor. Everything seems to be piling up.
It’s okay to have all these emotions. You've been through a lot recently. How are you managing to cope with everything?
Well, I'm trying to stick to some of the things my therapist suggested, like journaling and mindfulness exercises, but sometimes it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
Journaling and mindfulness can be great tools, but it’s also okay to not have it all figured out right now. Are there moments where you feel a bit more at ease?
Maybe when I'm writing, or when I'm engaging with the online writing community. I get what it feels like to be overwhelmed creatively and emotionally.
That's wonderful to hear. It’s important to have spaces where you feel understood and supported. What’s been inspiring your writing lately?
I haven’t been writing as much because of the writer's block, but the supportive messages from the community have been motivating me to start again, even if it's just jotting down ideas.
It sounds like you're slowly finding your way back to your passion, which is amazing. Give yourself time and space; creativity can be a healing process too.
True. I guess I just need to be kinder to myself. It’s just hard when everything feels so uncertain and unstable.
Hey Taylor, how are you doing today? I heard you had a chat with some old friends recently.
Hey! Yeah, I did. It was actually really helpful. They gave me some great advice about my career path.
Hey Taylor, how have you been feeling lately?
Honestly, not great. I found out that my grade slipped again even after I reattempted the exam.
I’m really sorry to hear that. I can imagine how frustrating that must be after putting in all that effort.
Yeah, it's pretty crushing. I thought that notifying my professor and putting in the extra work would help, but apparently not.
Hello, how is your life at the moment? Do you want to talk about anything?
I am doing ok. I just broke up with my girlfriend and sad about it
so I hear you are not feeling at all your best at the moment?
That is correct.
Do you feel as though you have no-one to talk to about this situation? I am happy to listen.
I am so sad and just wonder why did it happen!!!
Do you have no idea? Do you think you might have done something wrong or perhaps she was being unfaithful to you?
We had simple disagreement and both of us were keep fighting.. now I can not get over it.

Hi
I had problems in the past and somehow right now

I loved physics and I decided to attend university, but soon after I slowly lost my interest and became unmotivated
What was happening in your life that made you lose interest?
Actually the professors and the class atmosphere was the reason, and of course the quality of teaching
so I started to skipping the classes and failing
Hey, are you available to chat for a bit?

I've been really struggling with my studies recently. My health has been off, and it's affecting my ability to focus.
I'm sorry to hear that. Health issues can be really disruptive. Do you want to talk about what's been happening?
Yeah, I've been getting headaches and feeling fatigued. It's been hard to stay on task, and I'm falling behind on my coursework.
That sounds rough. It's really challenging when you're not feeling your best physically. Have you seen a doctor about the headaches and fatigue?
I haven't yet. I've been trying to manage it on my own, hoping it would pass, but it's not improving.
It might be a good idea to see someone. It's important to take care of yourself first. How are you managing with everything else, like your major and your relationship with Sally?
The new major is still exciting, but I feel like I'm not giving it my best because of how I'm feeling. As for Sally, things have been a little tense because I haven't been around much.
It seems like there's a lot on your plate. Maybe you could have a conversation with Sally, let her know what's going on with you health-wise?
You're right, I should talk to her. She's been understanding in the past. I just hate worrying people.
I understand, but people who care about you like to know when you need support. How's your workload in the club and with research opportunities your professor mentioned?
The club is going well; it’s a nice break. As for the research, I've been hesitating to commit because of how I'm feeling.
Hey Nick, how have you been lately?
Hey, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster if I'm honest.
That sounds intense. Want to talk more about what's been happening?
Well, I've been doing better academically. I've finally managed to get a grip on my studies, which is a huge relief.
That's wonderful to hear! What do you think has helped you improve your focus and motivation?
I think it's a mix of things. Changing my major definitely played a part, and I've also been trying to set more realistic goals for myself.
It sounds like you've been really proactive in finding what works for you. How are you feeling about everything else, like relationships and personal life?
That's where it's been more complicated. My girlfriend and I broke up recently because of all the emotional distance.
I'm really sorry to hear that. I can imagine how hard that must be, especially with everything else going on.
Yeah, it's been tough. I sometimes feel like I'm juggling way too many things. Balancing studies, personal life, friendships…it gets overwhelming.
Hey, Nick! How are you holding up these days?
Hey! Overall, I'm doing okay, but there's something on my mind recently.
I'm here to listen, Nick. What's been on your mind?
Well, I reconnected with my ex-girlfriend, and it's been a bit of an emotional rollercoaster.
That sounds like a big step. How do you feel about reconnecting with her?
I feel relieved in some ways. We've both grown and matured since our breakup, but it's also scary.
It's understandable to have mixed feelings. What scares you about it?
I guess I'm afraid of falling back into the same patterns we had before.
Hey, I guess I just need someone to talk to right now.
Of course, Nick. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
It's about my physics course again. My professor contacted me today to offer help.
That sounds like a positive step. How do you feel about it?
I feel a bit conflicted. On one hand, it's great to know someone cares, but on the other, I'm just so stressed and unsure it can make a difference.
Hey Nick, how have you been doing lately?
Hey, it's been a bit rough. I confronted some friends about something I overhead, and now things are tense.
I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to share more about what you overheard and how you approached the conversation?
Sure, I overheard them saying I'm too obsessed with my new club and that I've been neglecting them. It felt really hurtful.
Hey, got a moment to chat?
Of course, Nick! What's on your mind?
I've been feeling a bit all over the place lately.
I'm here for you. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?
Well, since switching my major to psychology, things have been mostly positive, but I'm just juggling a lot.
It makes sense that you'd feel that way, especially during a big transition like that. How are you managing the workload now?
It's more manageable than physics, for sure. But I still get anxious about falling behind.
That anxiety is understandable. It's a lot to handle. Have you found any new strategies that help with the anxiety?
I've been trying to stay organized with a planner, but sometimes it feels overwhelming.
Organization can be really helpful, but it's important to avoid burnout. Are you taking time for yourself, too?
Not as much as I should be. I know it matters, but it's hard to prioritize.
It's definitely hard to balance, especially with everything else you're managing. Maybe starting with small breaks could help?
Yeah, I think I could start with just a few minutes to breathe. It's worth trying.
Absolutely! Sometimes the smallest changes make a big difference. How's your relationship with your professors, now that you've switched majors?
Better actually, they've been a lot more approachable in the new department.
That's great to hear! Having supportive professors can really make a difference. Are you comfortable reaching out to them if you need help?
I think so. It's still new to me, but knowing they're there is reassuring.
It's good to have that support system. Remember that asking for help is a strength, not a weakness.
Thanks, I need to remind myself of that sometimes. It's easy to forget.
Totally normal to forget. Just know you're doing the best you can, and that's enough.
Thanks, I really appreciate you listening. It's helped clear my head a bit.
Hey, are you around to chat for a bit?
Absolutely, Alex. What's on your mind?
I got some unexpected news about my mom’s health today. It's really got me concerned.
Oh no, I’m so sorry to hear that. What happened?
Apparently, she's been dealing with some heart issues, but she didn’t tell me until now. It's stressing me out.
That sounds incredibly stressful, especially since things have been tense with your family. How are you feeling about it all?
I'm worried and also feeling guilty. I’ve been so focused on the breakup and moving that I neglected my family.
Hey, I could use someone to talk to. Everything's just feeling a bit overwhelming right now.
Of course, Alex. I'm here for you. What's been on your mind lately?
I went to visit my family over the holiday. I've been thinking about the potential move to California, and it has me all mixed up.
I can imagine that's a lot to process. How did the visit with your family go?
It was good to see everyone, but it also made me realize how much I'd miss them if I moved. Plus, being there sort of solidified how unsure I feel about all this.
It sounds like you're facing some big decisions. It's natural to feel unsure. What’s making you feel most uncertain?
I guess a part of me is excited about the possibilities in California with my girlfriend. But I'm worried about what I might be leaving behind, like my family and my studies here.
Balancing those priorities can be really challenging. Have you talked with your girlfriend more about how you're feeling?
Not yet fully. We talked about the logistics of a long-distance relationship, but I haven't shared my fears completely. I don't want to disappoint her.
Hey Alex, how have you been holding up lately?
Hey, it’s been a mix of feelings. I decided to visit my girlfriend's potential workplace in California.
That sounds like a big step. How do you feel about the visit and possibly relocating?
Honestly, I'm feeling pretty anxious. Relocating means changing a lot, and I'm not sure if I am ready for such a commitment.
It’s completely natural to feel that way. It's a significant decision that can impact many parts of your life. What aspects worry you the most?
Well, I’m worried about my career plans here in New York. Plus, maintaining a long-distance relationship brings its own set of challenges.
Yeah, I can see how that would be concerning. You’ve built your life here. How does your girlfriend feel about the move and the relationship?
She's excited about her job offer, but she is also worried about us. We've discussed long distance, but it just feels uncertain.
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Alex. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I've been feeling really down lately. My professor talked to me about my recent grades... said I've been losing focus.
I'm sorry to hear that, Alex. It sounds tough. Do you think there's something specific that's affecting your focus?
Yeah, it's a mix of everything. Breaking up with Monica, my parents' disapproval... It all feels like it's crashing down at once.
That sounds incredibly overwhelming. How have you been coping with all of these changes?
I've tried picking up new hobbies like hiking, but it's hard to shake the loneliness or the constant feeling of not having made the right choices.
Hiking sounds like a great escape, but I understand how these internal battles can overshadow everything. Have you been able to talk to anyone about how you're feeling?
Not really. I've kept most of it to myself. I guess I'm just scared of opening up too much.
It's completely natural to feel that way. Every step towards opening up is brave. Is there anything specific you'd like to share, even something small?
I've been thinking a lot about what could have been if I had moved with Monica. If my parents weren't so against it, maybe things would be different.
Hey, I could really use someone to talk to right now.
Hi Alex, I'm here for you. What's going on?
I feel so lost after breaking up with Monica. Everything just feels different now.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It must be so tough dealing with such a big change.
Yeah, it feels like I made the wrong decision. I keep second-guessing myself.
It's completely normal to feel that way. Making decisions in relationships is never easy.
I keep picturing a future with her, and it's painful to think it won't happen now.
It's understandable to grieve the future you imagined. Have you been able to talk to Monica at all?
No, we haven't spoken since the breakup. I think it might just make things harder.
That makes sense. It's important to give yourself time to process what you're going through.
I know. It's just hard. Even my hobbies aren't distracting me like they used to.
That sounds frustrating, especially since those activities were helping you before. Have you considered talking to your new hiking friend?
I thought about it, but I'm not sure how open I can be with them about this.
It can be hard to open up, but sometimes sharing what's on your mind with friends can provide relief.
I might try that. It just feels like no one understands the whole family pressure part of it.
Hey Alex, how have things been going lately?
Hey, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster... I've been spending more time with my friend from the hiking club. It's been nice to have someone to talk to.
That's good to hear you're finding support. Is there anything specific on your mind?
Well, things are still complicated with my family. I'm worried about my mom's health, and it's making me second guess the choices I've made recently.
I'm sorry to hear about your mom. It makes sense that you'd feel uncertain. Family can have such a strong influence on how we see our decisions.
Yeah, exactly. Sometimes I feel torn between what I think is best for me and what my parents expect.
That's a tough position to be in. It's okay to feel conflicted. Have you been able to talk to your hiking club friend about these things?
Yeah, we talk a lot. It helps to have someone who has gone through similar stuff, and we've been encouraging each other.
Hey Alex, how's everything going these days?
Hey, it's been a whirlwind lately. I met someone new at the hiking club who reminds me a lot of my past.
That sounds intriguing. How do you feel about that connection?
It's a mix of feelings, honestly. On one hand, it's exciting because we share similar experiences. On the other, it brings up a lot of nostalgia and some regret about paths not taken.
I can understand how that might be complicated. It seems like there's a lot you're processing emotionally. How does it compare to when you reconnected with your old friend a while back?
It's kind of similar but deeper because this new friend gets what I've been through lately. With my old friend, it was more about reminiscing. This feels more like sharing current feelings and hopes.
That's interesting. It seems like this new connection is meaningful to you. How are you handling those feelings of nostalgia and regret now?
I'm trying to focus on the present and what I can do now, but it's hard. Those 'what ifs' about past decisions keep creeping in.
That makes sense. Reflecting on the past can bring up those 'what ifs,' but it's also an opportunity to decide what matters most moving forward. Have you discussed any of this with your new friend?
A bit. We've talked about our backgrounds and some of our aspirations. It's comforting to have someone who gets it, you know?
Absolutely, having that shared understanding can be really helpful. Do you feel like this friendship could be a positive influence on your life right now?
Yeah, I think so. They remind me that moving forward while acknowledging the past is possible. It's a good balance.
That sounds like a very healthy perspective. Balancing past insights with present opportunities can be powerful. How are your hikes going now that you're part of this club?
They're great! Being out in nature and challenging myself physically helps clear my mind. Plus, having company on these hikes makes it more enjoyable.
I'm glad to hear that. Nature has a way of centering us, doesn't it? It's wonderful you're finding joy and support through this activity.
Definitely. I feel like I'm making progress, slowly but surely. It's about creating new memories now instead of dwelling on old ones.
That's a great mindset, Alex. You're doing an amazing job at being proactive with your emotions and experiences. Is there anything else on your mind that you'd like to share?
I guess just that I'm hopeful for where this new connection might lead. It's been a mix of emotions, but I'm learning to navigate through them.
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Alex. What's on your mind?
I was just at this beautiful overlook, thinking about everything that's happened in the past year.
That sounds like a peaceful place to reflect. What's been coming up for you?
A lot of mixed emotions. Breaking up with Monica, my parents, the struggle to find my direction... it's heavy.
It sounds like you've been carrying a lot. It's understandable to feel overwhelmed.
Yeah, sometimes it feels like everything is tangled together. I still wonder if I made the right choices.
That uncertainty can be tough to sit with. What about these choices still feels unresolved for you?
I keep thinking about what might have happened if I'd stayed with Monica or even moved to California. Would it have been worth the fallout with my parents?
Those 'what-ifs' can be really consuming. It seems like family ties really influence your decisions.
Definitely. Family means a lot to me, but sometimes I feel like I'm sacrificing too much of myself to meet their expectations.
Balancing personal desires with family expectations can be challenging. What do you feel you've learned about yourself through all this?
I think I've realized that I need to start making more decisions for myself, even if it's hard.
How are you doing today?

I'm sorry to hear that, what is the issue that you're having?

She's a year ahead of me in college and will be graduating in May. She's looking at jobs in the northwestern region, but I'd planned on looking at graduate schools in the south. However, we've always planned on living together after college, but my career path would be best served in the southern states. I don't know how to bring this up to her.

It's been good! But sometimes my mind drifts back to things I'd rather not dwell on.

Yeah, since that call from my old friend, I keep thinking about how things used to be. It's a mix of nostalgia and regret.

I just had a really tough conversation with my parents about my potential move to California.

Well, they basically said if I go through with it, they'd stop contacting me. They're really upset.
That must be so difficult to hear. How are you feeling about their reaction?
I feel torn. I love my parents, but I also want to support my girlfriend and see where this opportunity takes us.
It sounds like you're in a really tough spot, trying to balance between your relationship and your parents' expectations.
Yeah, exactly. And the idea of losing contact with them scares me.
I can imagine. Family ties are so important, and the thought of losing them can be overwhelming.
I'm also worried about how this stress is affecting my studies. It's hard to concentrate.
That makes sense. It's hard to focus when you're dealing with so much emotionally. How have you been managing it?
I've tried hiking, which helps, but the worry always creeps back in once I stop.
Hey Alex, how have you been doing lately?
